### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1739f71879f27d10c07fbde77fcf0728ed9abb81` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: 1/1 CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER
Reviewed-by: session_01JbZnqu8bt6YqfJsr9vaFb3 (isolated reviewer subagent; no direction taken from the dispatching seat)
Reviewed at 2026-09-20T09:02Z · PR #19270 (draft) for card #18407 · base `origin/main` `1739f71879`; control tree `7d0f911da9` = the merge-base, and the two commits between them touch only `field.zod.ts`, a repeater test, a changeset and a docs page — none of the gate, the manifest, the baseline or `packages/spec/package.json`.

```
49f7e0d23ea931a925a5ec0f672bf205ac639190
```

Evidence: the card body and its triage ruling, the PR (diff, body, check-runs, one job log), `origin/main`, objectui at the pinned sha and at its newest `main`, and the published `@object-ui/*` 17.6.0 tarballs. Seat comments were read; nothing was adopted from them — every number below is re-taken.

① **Serves the card, and only that — the half that can be delivered here.**
- The diff is exactly two files, `packages/spec/scripts/check-react-blocks-declaration-parity.ts` and its `.test.ts`; `git diff --name-only 7d0f911da9..49f7e0d23e` lists nothing else — no manifest, no provenance record, no `.objectui-sha`, no baseline, no changeset.
- The card's zero, re-taken on `origin/main`: `sdui.manifest.json` has 57 components; names containing "tree" → `[]`; LIT CONTROL on the same parse, names starting `object-` → object-grid, object-form, object-master-detail-form, object-kanban, object-calendar, object-gantt, object-timeline, object-map, object-metric, object-chart, object-pivot (11). The gate on `origin/main` under CI's exact invocation (`--baseline react-declaration-parity.baseline.json --strict`) prints `✗ object-tree: NO component in the manifest` and then `✓ no new DECLARATION divergence` → **exit 0**; plain `--strict` on the same tree → **exit 1**. The card's sharp half ("cannot fail") reproduces.
- Regeneration re-measured rather than taken: built `packages/sdui-parser/dist`, installed the 17 published `@object-ui/*` 17.6.0 packages from npm (the version `packages/core/package.json` declares at objectui `53ded82b`, read through `OBJECTUI_ROOT`), ran `node scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs --modules-root …` on the control tree: `✓ wrote sdui.manifest.json (57 components, 66910 bytes, sha256 49211fee7792…)`; `git hash-object` before = after = `origin/main` = `78f870e42fe9`; `git status` shows only `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json` (its date-only field). In the regenerated file, names containing "tree" → `[]`, LIT CONTROL 11 `object-` names. **Byte-identical no-op, confirmed.**
- Why it is absent, re-measured with my own probe on that same install: `getAllConfigs()` 494 configs — tree names `ui:tree-view`, `plugin-tree:object-tree`, `view:tree` (LIT CONTROL, grid names: 6); `getPublicConfigs()` 57 — tree names `[]` (LIT CONTROL: `object-grid`, `grid`); exported `PUBLIC_BLOCKS` 57 — tree `[]` (LIT CONTROL: `object-grid`, `grid`); `getConfig('object-tree')` → registered, `tier=undefined`, `namespace=plugin-tree`, inputs `objectName, tree`. At objectui source `53ded82b` (shallow clone, commit present): `packages/plugin-tree/src/index.tsx` registers `'object-tree'` at line 35 (namespace `plugin-tree`) and `'tree'` at line 42 (namespace `view`), neither with a `tier`; `packages/core/src/registry/public-blocks.ts` has 57 entries, a tree grep exits 1, LIT CONTROL `'object-grid'` line 28 and `'grid'` line 100; `Registry.ts` public-tier paths at lines 821 (`PUBLIC_BLOCKS`), 824 and 828 (`tier === 'public'` on the config and on the entry meta) — none can fire. Also checked what the PR did not: objectui's newest `main` (`078f2e4f`) still has no tree entry in `PUBLIC_BLOCKS`, still registers without a tier, and `@object-ui/core` is still 17.6.0 — a pin bump to today's head would not produce the entry either.
- Scope verdict: the triage ruling names two deliverables — an `object-tree` entry in the manifest, and "spec row with no manifest row" going red on its own. The first is not producible from this repository: both producers faithfully serialise a public tier that does not carry the block, so the cure is objectui's curation or the spec row, a decision. The diff delivers the second, touches nothing else, and is declared `Part of`, not a close. Not a substitution.

② **`Clause-②: no` is a true reading of this diff.**
- `@objectstack/spec` `files[]` at the head (byte-identical to main): `dist, json-schema, liveness, prompts, llms.txt, README.md, src/**/*.zod.ts, CHANGELOG.md, api-surface, api-surface-declarations, spec-changes.json` — `scripts/` in none. Positive control on the same manifest: `npm pack --dry-run` at the head packs 293 entries, **0** under `scripts/` and 0 matching `declaration-parity`, while `src/ui/component.zod.ts`, `src/ui/page.zod.ts` and `README.md` are packed.
- `exports` (19 keys) names no `scripts/` path, and nothing under `packages/spec/src` imports either changed file (the only `src → scripts` imports are three test files pulling `scripts/lib/export-origins-testkit`, untouched). No published payload gains a key, no closed set moves, no export or registry entry moves. The one accept-set that narrows is the CI gate's own `--update`, which is tooling, not a published contract. `skip-changeset` is the label AGENTS.md assigns to exactly this.

③ **Sound, and nothing is left vacuous — with one body error and two costs to name.**
- Real exit codes, this act:

| run | head `49f7e0d2` | control `7d0f911d` |
|:--|:--:|:--:|
| gate `--baseline react-declaration-parity.baseline.json --strict` (CI's line) | **1** — `object-tree: … NO baseline row` | **0** — same `✗` line, then `✓ no new` |
| gate plain `--strict` | **1** | **1** |
| the gate's own suite (`vitest run --project local`, that file) | **0** — 36 passed | 30 tests in the file |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` (incl. `check:scripts-typecheck`, `check:test-typecheck`) | **0** | — |

- (a) Fixtures. Verified by swapping one file at a time between the two trees in their own worktrees (blobs checked: gate `6f6ccc1a` ↔ `8bda7e2d`, test `f53bfe53` ↔ `20bbd1ae`). **Main's old test file against the head gate: 6 failed / 24 passed** — `exits 0 when the manifest matches the accepted baseline`, `carries the caveat on a clean baseline ratchet too`, `a block not yet in the baseline is additive`, `accepts a node-level key … (dataSource)`, `accepts the other node-level key … (className)`, `applies to the react-block half too` — each a one-component-manifest fixture expecting a clean ratchet; they passed on main only because twelve absent, unbaselined blocks could not regress. **Head's test file against the main gate: 4 failed / 32 passed** — exactly the four `#18407` pins (absent block with no baseline row is a regression; the failure text sends the reader upstream; a `missing: true` row does not buy silence; `--update` refuses), with both CONTROL cases green. The repaired fixtures discriminate in both directions. `evaluatedBlockTypes()` carries its own lit control (it throws unless `object-form`, `list-view` and `object-grid` are read off the report); the head run evaluates 13 blocks, the baseline has 9 rows, the four without a row are object-gantt, object-map, object-timeline and object-tree, and only object-tree is absent from the manifest — blast radius one block, as the PR says.
- (b) Landing. ⚠️ The PR body says the red lands in `Lint & Repo Gates`. **It does not.** In `lint.yml` at `origin/main` the parity step (line 6344) is inside job `typecheck-consumers` (`Type Check · consumer gates`), a lane of the aggregate `typecheck` (`TypeScript Type Check`, `needs:` all four lanes); `Lint & Repo Gates` (job `lint`) carries `check-sdui-manifest.mjs`, not this gate. The PR's own CI on this head agrees: `Type Check · consumer gates` → failure, its log ending in the `object-tree … NO baseline row` block and `Exit status 1`; `TypeScript Type Check` → failure. The ruleset on `main` (REST, HTTP 200) lists seven required contexts, and `TypeScript Type Check` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are both among them, so the consequence the body draws holds — merged as-is, a required context is red on every later PR and on `main`'s own runs, and the queue lands nothing until objectui exposes the block or the spec row is dropped — but the context it names is wrong. ⛔ Not patched by this review; correct it on the next body edit the seat must make anyway (readying the draft). The hold is the draft flag alone; that decision is outside this review and is not the verdict.
- (c) Circumvention, probed on the real manifest at the head: a hand-written baseline row `object-tree: {missing: false}` → **exit 1** (`block vanished from the manifest`); a hand-written `{missing: true}` row → **exit 1** (`does NOT accept this`); the reflex, `--update` against a copy of the committed baseline → **exit 1**, `refusing to write a baseline while 1 block(s) have NO component … - object-tree`, and the copy's sha256 is unchanged before and after. Control, main's gate, same command → **exit 0**, `wrote declaration-parity baseline … (13 blocks)`, and the written file carries `object-tree: {registryOnly: [], missing: true}` — the acceptance the head refuses to mint. What remains is outside the gate: editing the gate or the workflow step, hand-editing `sdui.manifest.json` (caught by `check-sdui-manifest.mjs` sha256-vs-record in the lint job) or removing the `ComponentPropsMap` row — each visible in a diff, none a baseline-side silence.
- Two costs, named, not blocking: while any block is missing, `--update` refuses to write **anything**, so a legitimate new registry-only accept on another block needs a hand edit of the baseline until `object-tree` is resolved (the failure text says so); and the committed baseline's `_comment` still describes the old semantics ("flags only NEW registry-only inputs or newly-missing blocks") and cannot be refreshed through `--update` for the same reason.

Measured first-hand in this act: the card's zero and its lit controls on `origin/main`; the manifest regeneration on the control tree from a fresh npm install of the published 17.6.0 set and the hash comparison; the registry probe on that install (all / public / `PUBLIC_BLOCKS` / `getConfig`) with grid controls; the objectui readings at the pinned sha and at newest `main`; `files[]`, `exports` and `npm pack --dry-run`; both gate modes on both trees; the head suite and typecheck; both one-file-swap ablations; the three baseline and `--update` probes with a main control; the `lint.yml` job graph, the ruleset's required contexts, the PR's check-run conclusions and one job log.
Taken from someone else's reading and NOT verified: the PR's two surgical ablations through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (whole-file swaps were run instead); its full `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` (14649 tests), whole-repo eslint, `pnpm build` and the "53 derived gate families" — NOT MEASURED here; the browser route (`pnpm sdui:manifest`, Playwright plus a vendored objectui build) — NOT MEASURED, so #17735's cell is untouched by this review; the `Registry.ts` public-tier paths were read as source and exercised only through the published dist.

PASS
